section_summary: This section follows U.S. efforts to secure a treaty restricting Japanese salmon fishing in Bristol Bay. Japanese officials declined negotiations while repeatedly saying they had issued no salmon fishing licenses near Alaska. The later documents cover reports of Japanese vessels, a planned fisheries survey, public concern about salmon stocks, and an unconfirmed report that the Chichibu Maru was using salmon gill nets.

subfiles.title: Telegram on Japan’s response to proposed salmon fishing negotiations
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese reluctance to negotiate restrictions on offshore salmon packing.
subfiles.summary: Neville describes Japan’s wish to retain discretion over fishing licenses and asks for instructions.

subfiles.title: Commerce request for another approach to Japan
subfiles.about: Urges renewed efforts to secure a fisheries treaty.
subfiles.summary: Commerce cites the potential danger to Alaskan salmon fisheries and urges prompt treaty negotiations.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo to await further directions
subfiles.about: Reports discussion with the Japanese Ambassador and suspends further embassy action.
subfiles.summary: The Ambassador will present U.S. views to Tokyo; the Embassy should await instructions.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Commerce on proposed convention
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Describes the new approach made through the Japanese Ambassador.
subfiles.summary: State asked the Ambassador to convey the benefits of a convention and directed the chargé in Tokyo to await further instructions.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for file 894.628/137
subfiles.about: Records a later charge of the file.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge slip for file 894.628/137.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs summary of Tokyo despatch 1558
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japan’s refusal to discuss a salmon fishing convention.
subfiles.summary: The division notes continued Japanese refusal of salmon licenses, Neville’s hope for reconsideration, and Sayre’s approach to the Ambassador.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch 1558 on fisheries
subfiles.about: Details Japanese reasons for declining salmon fishing negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Neville reports that Japanese officials consider the proposed treaty insufficiently important and want freedom over future licensing. They say no offshore salmon fishing is currently intended near Alaska. He encloses a memorandum of his November 12 conversation.

subfiles.title: Neville–Horinouchi conversation on Bristol Bay salmon fishing
subfiles.about: Records Japan’s refusal to negotiate and its assurances about licensing.
subfiles.summary: Horinouchi says Japanese crab interests are limited and the government wants to retain freedom to license fishing across a large area. Neville stresses the risk to American salmon canneries. Horinouchi says earlier salmon license applications were refused and promises further consultation, without committing Japan to a treaty.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Tokyo despatch 1558 to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards Neville’s fuller account of the Japanese response.
subfiles.summary: Encloses despatch 1558 confirming Japan’s reluctance to negotiate.

subfiles.title: Proposed convention with Japan to regulate Bristol Bay fishing
subfiles.about: Reviews the history and recommends another approach to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum describes concern that offshore Japanese fishing could damage Bristol Bay red salmon runs and American investment. It recounts unsuccessful 1930 talks, proposed tariff concessions, and Japan’s reluctance in 1935. It recommends asking the Japanese Ambassador to support an agreement, drawing an analogy with bilateral trade understandings.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of the renewed approach
subfiles.about: Acknowledges State’s discussion with the Japanese Ambassador.
subfiles.summary: Commerce welcomes the new approach and awaits Japan’s response.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese fishery subsidies
subfiles.about: Points to a letter concerning Japan’s interest in the Oriental Development Company.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a letter suggesting Japanese government support for its fishery industry.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment of despatch 1558
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the Tokyo despatch.
subfiles.summary: Commerce notes Japan’s reluctance to negotiate and expresses interest in the information.

subfiles.title: Yoshizawa–Sayre conversation on the proposed treaty
subfiles.about: Records Japan’s definitive refusal to negotiate a salmon fishing treaty.
subfiles.summary: Yoshizawa says Japan sees no acceptable exchange for negotiations but continues to discourage salmon fishing in the area. Sayre treats the answer as closing the proposal.

subfiles.title: State Department report to Commerce on Japan’s refusal
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Conveys Japan’s response and invites Commerce’s comments.
subfiles.summary: Japan declines treaty negotiations while saying it still discourages salmon fishing near Alaska.

subfiles.title: Copy of December 30 Yoshizawa–Sayre conversation
subfiles.about: Provides the detailed record of Japan’s final response.
subfiles.summary: Yoshizawa repeats that Japan will not negotiate but will discourage salmon fishing; Sayre accepts the response as final.

subfiles.title: Instruction requesting Ambassador Grew’s assessment
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Seeks Tokyo’s further views after Japan’s rejection.
subfiles.summary: State sends the conversation memorandum and asks Grew for suggestions or comments.

subfiles.title: Commerce acknowledgment that treaty talks are closed
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Japan’s refusal and offers to report later developments.
subfiles.summary: Commerce notes the matter is closed for the present and promises relevant updates.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese interest in South Seas fisheries
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report from Wellington.
subfiles.summary: Points to a report on concern about Japanese activity in South Seas fisheries.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs summary of Grew’s despatch
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokyo’s view of future fisheries negotiations.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy expects delay until Soviet–Japanese disputes ease and speculates about a fur seal treaty exchange.

subfiles.title: Grew despatch 1698 on the proposed Alaskan salmon treaty
subfiles.about: Assesses prospects for renewed fisheries negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Grew doubts Japan will negotiate while its fishing dispute with the Soviet Union continues. He considers it unlikely that Japan will encourage salmon fishing near Alaska, and speculates that it might later trade a salmon restriction for fur seal treaty changes.

subfiles.title: Transmission of despatch 1698 to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew’s assessment of the treaty proposal.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the February 21 Tokyo despatch for Commerce’s information.

subfiles.title: Naval Operations forwarding note
subfiles.from: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.about: Forwards material on Japanese activity in Alaskan waters.
subfiles.summary: Cover note for extracts from Bering Sea Patrol reports.

subfiles.title: Extracts from Bering Sea Patrol reports
subfiles.to: Office of the Chief of Naval Operations
subfiles.about: Describes observed Japanese vessel activity near Aleutian islands.
subfiles.summary: The extracts describe Japanese vessels, suspected shore approaches and photography, possible interest in sea otters, and interference from fishing gear. Some claims are explicitly suspicions rather than verified findings.

subfiles.title: Bower–Turner telephone conversation about salmon fishing reports
subfiles.about: Records Commerce’s request to check reports of Japanese salmon licenses.
subfiles.summary: Bower cites reports from McGovern and a proposed trade journal article. Despite earlier Japanese assurances, he asks State to verify whether policy has changed.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Tokyo about alleged salmon licenses
subfiles.about: Requests permission to publicize Japanese assurances about salmon licenses.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Embassy to check whether Japan objects to sharing its earlier assurances with Alaskan fishing interests.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram denying salmon licenses
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s renewed denial of offshore salmon fishing licenses.
subfiles.summary: Japan says no licenses have been issued or contemplated and permits the assurance to be shared.

subfiles.title: State Department transmission of Tokyo’s denial
subfiles.about: Sends Commerce the Embassy’s rebuttal of unofficial reports.
subfiles.summary: Hull encloses the March 31 telegram and says the salmon fishing report lacks factual support.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on despatch 1764
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japan’s denial of salmon licenses.
subfiles.summary: Notes that despatch 1764 confirms the Embassy’s earlier telegram.

subfiles.title: Grew despatch 1764 on alleged Alaskan salmon fishing
subfiles.about: Forwards two conversations with the Japanese Foreign Office.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that Japan denies issuing salmon licenses, has no present intention to do so, and permits disclosure of this information.

subfiles.title: Neville–Horinouchi conversation on rumored fishing
subfiles.about: Seeks verification of reports of Japanese salmon fishing.
subfiles.summary: Horinouchi doubts licenses were issued and promises to check with the Fisheries Bureau.

subfiles.title: Horinouchi’s telephone confirmation
subfiles.about: Records the Fisheries Bureau’s denial of licenses.
subfiles.summary: Horinouchi says no salmon licenses were issued or planned and authorizes disclosure.

subfiles.title: Bureau of Fisheries letter to McGovern
subfiles.about: Advises against publishing an alarming article on Japanese salmon fishing.
subfiles.summary: Bell favors handling the matter through official channels and keeping negotiations confidential.

subfiles.title: McGovern letter to Fishery Advisory Committee
subfiles.about: Requests committee discussion of an alleged Japanese threat to Bristol Bay salmon.
subfiles.summary: McGovern cites Japanese license demands and a planned Pacific Fisherman article.

subfiles.title: Bureau of Fisheries letter to Miller Freeman
subfiles.about: Explains concern over publication of an unverified salmon fishing story.
subfiles.summary: Bell says the proposed story needs verification and that publicity could hinder official discussions.

subfiles.title: Miller Freeman’s history of Japanese Pacific fisheries
subfiles.about: Argues for stronger U.S. action on Japanese fishing.
subfiles.summary: Freeman recounts past disputes in Alaska and on the Pacific coast, alleges displacement of American cod fishermen, and criticizes U.S. inaction and naval intelligence. He urges an effective response to Japanese activity in Bristol Bay.

subfiles.title: Bell letter asking Gray to withhold article
subfiles.about: Challenges an unverified report and asks that publication be delayed.
subfiles.summary: Bell says official information shows no Japanese salmon licenses and warns that the proposed article could hinder future negotiations. He acknowledges Japanese crab operations but says no deliberate salmon canning has been established.

subfiles.title: Gray letter urging action to protect Bristol Bay salmon
subfiles.about: Asks about U.S. policy toward alleged Japanese salmon fishing.
subfiles.summary: Gray urges diplomacy and patrols to protect Bristol Bay salmon runs.

subfiles.title: Proposed Pacific Fisherman article on Japanese operations
subfiles.about: Reports alleged Japanese salmon packing near the Alaska Peninsula.
subfiles.summary: The draft alleges a salmon pack and urges protection of Bristol Bay stocks; its claim was disputed by officials.

subfiles.title: State note on New York Times fishing report
subfiles.about: Records consultation with Bower about a reported Japanese survey.
subfiles.summary: Bower agrees that the Embassy should seek further information promptly.

subfiles.title: Japanese plan to fish off Alaska
subfiles.about: Reports a planned Japanese trawler survey near Alaska.
subfiles.summary: The clipping says the Tenyo Maru will investigate offshore fishing prospects over a three-year program.

subfiles.title: State inquiry to Tokyo about Tenyo Maru report
subfiles.about: Requests comment on the reported Japanese fishing survey.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Embassy to investigate a New York Times report of planned offshore exploration.

subfiles.title: Bureau of Fisheries letter to Gray on the survey
subfiles.about: Shares official information on a Japanese survey near Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Bell says the Fisheries Bureau plans a three-season investigation, with no private ventures authorized.

subfiles.title: Instructions concerning Professor Konda’s Bristol Bay visit
subfiles.about: Asks field staff to assist and learn about Konda’s visit.
subfiles.summary: Bell requests courtesies for Konda and prompt reports on his objectives.

subfiles.title: Bell acknowledgment of Allen’s report on Konda
subfiles.about: Responds to news of Konda’s trip to Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Bell says Bureau staff will meet Konda courteously and seek information about his purpose.

subfiles.title: Allen report on Professor Konda
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese professor’s trip to Bristol Bay.
subfiles.summary: Allen says Konda describes his visit as promoting peaceful settlement of fisheries issues.

subfiles.title: New Zealand commentary on Japanese South Seas fisheries
subfiles.about: Voices concern about Japanese fisheries expansion in southern waters.
subfiles.summary: The extract calls for New Zealand to inquire into Japan’s fishing and naval plans.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on Japanese Bristol Bay investigation
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s plan to study fish runs and tidal flows.
subfiles.summary: A Japanese official says a chartered vessel will conduct a likely three-season survey, with no private ventures authorized.

subfiles.title: Transmission of survey telegram to the Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew’s report on the Japanese survey.
subfiles.summary: Hull sends the Navy the June 4 telegram prompted by the Tenyo Maru news report.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram identifying Tenyo Maru survey vessels
subfiles.about: Gives vessel details and the stated limits of Japan’s survey.
subfiles.summary: The Tenyo Maru and an auxiliary boat will study fish distribution and sea conditions on the high seas without entering U.S. waters.

subfiles.title: State inquiry about Chichibu Maru gill nets
subfiles.about: Requests information on a reported Japanese salmon fishing vessel.
subfiles.summary: State asks Tokyo to investigate a report that Chichibu Maru used salmon gill nets in Bristol Bay.

subfiles.title: State note on the June survey and possible legal response
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s survey and the limits of possible U.S. protest.
subfiles.summary: State officers discuss the survey with Bower and conclude a protest would need evidence of serious injury to U.S. salmon resources. They view the survey as potentially preparatory to Japanese fishing if access to Russian waters becomes less attractive, but agree to await developments.

subfiles.title: Bell letter defending reliance on Japanese assurances
subfiles.about: Responds to Gray’s skepticism about Japanese fishing licenses.
subfiles.summary: Bell says there is no evidence that Japanese vessels have harmed salmon runs and trusts State to respond to any verified threat.

subfiles.title: Gray letter questioning Japanese assurances
subfiles.about: Urges close scrutiny of Japanese fishing near Alaska.
subfiles.summary: Gray suspects incidental salmon catches and asks the government to establish and enforce clear principles.

subfiles.title: Bell letter on licensed Japanese crab vessels
subfiles.about: Shares Embassy information about Japanese crab fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Bell says the licensed vessels are assigned to crab fishing and fish meal, giving no present cause for salmon concern.

subfiles.title: Tokyo reply on Chichibu Maru
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s initial lack of information about Chichibu Maru.
subfiles.summary: Foreign Office officials say they know nothing of the vessel’s activity and will investigate.

subfiles.title: State note on patrol report of Chichibu Maru
subfiles.about: Assesses an uncorroborated report of salmon gear.
subfiles.summary: Bower doubts the report and seeks corroboration; crab nets may have been mistaken for salmon nets.

subfiles.title: Bureau of Fisheries request for corroboration
subfiles.about: Seeks evidence for a patrol report that Chichibu Maru used salmon gill nets.
subfiles.summary: Jackson contrasts the report with Japanese licensing assurances and asks for corroborative information.
